name: Flamerush Rider
oracle_text:
Whenever this creature attacks, create a token that's a copy of another target attacking creature and that's tapped and attacking. Exile the token at end of combat.
Dash {2}{R}{R} (You may cast this spell for its dash cost. If you do, it gains haste, and it's returned from the battlefield to its owner's hand at the beginning of the next end step.)
blocked_sentences: Exile the token at end of combat.

needs.what: A way to schedule an effect for the end of combat step -- either an `end_of_combat` entry in `turn.DELAY_STEPS` mapping to the already-existing `Step.END_OF_COMBAT`, so `{"op": "delay", "step": "end_of_combat", "effects": [...]}` fires there, or an `end_of_combat` member of `trigger_events` fired from the same site `postcombat_main` and `begin_combat` are. The delay form is the one this card wants, because "Exile the token at end of combat" is a delayed trigger created by the attack trigger's resolution and not a standing ability. It needs to fire once per combat rather than once per turn, since `Step.END_OF_COMBAT` is re-entered by every extra combat phase, and a delayed trigger scheduled during the combat damage step of one combat must fire at the end of *that* combat rather than waiting for the next turn's.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `Step.END_OF_COMBAT` (= 9) already exists in `engine/enums.py` and the turn walk passes through it, but nothing can be attached to it: `turn.DELAY_STEPS` maps only `upkeep`, `draw_step`, `begin_combat` and `end_step`, and `delay`'s step is matched against that table alone, so `{"step": "end_of_combat"}` silently never becomes due and the token would live forever. The nearest reachable step from `trigger_events` is `end_step`, and substituting it is wrong in a way that matters on exactly this card: the copy would survive the entire postcombat main phase, so it could be sacrificed, tapped for an ability, or attack again in an extra combat -- the printed exile-at-end-of-combat is what stops all of that. `exile` itself carries only `until_leaves` (the O-Ring link) and `playable_this_turn`; neither is a timing.

needs.what: A way for a later effect to name the token an earlier effect just created -- an `as` field on `create_token` and `copy_permanent` that records the new tokens' oids into `ctx.bindings`, exactly as `sacrifice`'s `as` records the objects it consumed, so a following `delay` can carry `{"objects": {"binding": "the_token"}}` into its scheduled `exile`. `delay` already captures `dict(ctx.bindings)` when it schedules, so the binding would survive to the later step with no further work; the missing half is only that the two token-creating ops write nothing down.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `op_create_token` and `op_copy_permanent` in `effects/ops_board.py` both call `create_token(...)` and discard its result -- neither reads an `as` key -- so there is no binding for the `binding` / `exclude_binding` selector keys or the `binding` value key to read, even though those keys exist and `sacrifice` demonstrates the pattern. Reconstructing the token from a selector instead does not work: `is_token` matches every token you control, and `{"is_token": true, "attacking": true}` would also catch tokens made by anything else attacking that turn, so a second Flamerush Rider trigger, or any other token-making attack trigger, makes the card exile the wrong object. `exiled_with` and `haunted_by` link back to a *source*, not to objects an effect produced. `snapshot` copies characteristics off an object for later reading, not an identity a later effect can act on.
